en.html:
She did not remember where she had walked, or how.

When she noticed, Ichijou was already in a back street at night. Anything annoying in her way she moved aside without a thought, and kept going.

No destination. No errand. Yet she did not feel like going back to her <ruby>lodgings<rt>roost</rt></ruby> either.

Her brain was boiling.

Damn it.

One thing only was in her head.

That man.

Kageaki Minato.

At first she had taken him for a boring coward. Then she had seen him fight in a sword-armor.

She had believed in him. Burned with admiration.

And today she had been made to understand that all of it was a mistake.

Why, damn it.

Whatever she thought, it ended up set hard around that one question.

He had been brilliant. He had been dazzling.

Because she had seen a light in him.

He had been an answer. To a question that she once could not even find the loose end of.

Rokuhara. The Silver Star... A giant evil with no way to resist it: how was one to stand against that?

<ruby>Compromise<rt>・・</rt></ruby>, as so many people do? Say that what exists cannot be helped, and what cannot be done cannot be done? Or else refuse it to the end, and <ruby>only<rt>・・</rt></ruby> deny it?

Say with your mouth that you accept no evil, ignore the giant evil you cannot touch, pick only the small evils you can fight, and be satisfied. ...That was Ichijou before she met him. Though she had never really been satisfied.

Then a warrior in red armor had thrown light on that torment.

Fight, that was all.

If you cannot forgive it, fight it.

That the enemy is too strong, that you cannot win however you try: none of that matters.

He had never thought of such things. No, he had thought of them, but <ruby>only after he had decided to fight<rt>・・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>.

If you have to fight, you fight. The odds of winning come after.

That this was enough, his figure had shown her, challenging even a Rokuhara warrior without fear.

...And yet.

何処をどう歩いたのかは覚えていない。

　気付けば一条は夜の裏通りに踏み入っていた。
　何やら目障りなモノを適当にどかしつつ、進む。

　あてはない。用事もない。
　だが、<ruby>住処<rt>ねぐら</rt></ruby>に戻りたい気分ではなかった。

　脳漿が煮え立っている。

　――畜生。

　思う事はただ一つ。
　あの男。

　湊斗景明。

　最初はつまらない腰抜けだと思って。
　その後、劒冑を纏って戦う姿を見て。

　信じて。
　焦がれて。

　今日。
　全てが勘違いだったのだと、思い知らされた。

　――なんでだよ。

　想念は結局、その一言に凝固した。

　輝かしかったのだ。
　眩しかったのだ。

　そこに一つの光を見たから。

　彼は、答えだった。
　嘗ては解く糸口すら見えなかった問いへの。

　六波羅、銀星号……
　抗いようとてない強大な悪に、どう立ち向かうべき
なのか？

　多くの人々がそうしているように、<ruby>妥協<rt>・・</rt></ruby>するか――
有るものはしょうがないのだ、どうしようもないもの
はどうしようもないのだ、と。
　それとも、あくまで否定するか――否定<ruby>だけ<rt>・・</rt></ruby>するか。

　悪を認めないと口では言いつつ、手の出せない巨悪
は放置して、戦える小悪だけを選んで相手取り、満足
する。……彼に出会う前の一条がそうだった。
　決して満足はしていなかったけれども。

　その煩悶に、赤い甲鉄の武者が光をあてた。
　――戦えばいいのだ、と。

　許せないなら、戦えばいい。

　相手が強過ぎるとか、
　どうやっても勝てないとか、
　そんなことは関係がない。

　彼は、そんなことを考えなかった。
　いや、考えてはいた――<ruby>戦うと決めた後で<rt>・・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>。

　戦わねばならないなら、戦うのだ。
　勝算などはその次だ。

　それで良いのだと、示してくれた。
　あの、六波羅の武者にも敢然と挑んだ姿が。

　……だというのに。

en.html:
Her thoughts went one full circle and came back to the start. Exactly like her feet, going round the same place again and again.

Kageaki Minato was simply a murderer.
He killed without choosing between good and bad.

She could not believe it. She did not want to believe it.

But she could not doubt it either. His confession was too heavy to be a lie.

That was the fact.

...She could make no sense of any of it.

She almost wanted to throw everything away. Forget all of it, and start over from zero in some other town.

If she did, nobody could blame her.

Then... could she do it?
Could Ichijou Ayane do that?

Impossible.

ja.html:
考えは一周して元に戻る。
　同じ場所をぐるぐる回っている一条の足と同じよう
に。

　
　　　　　湊斗景明はただの殺人者。
　　　　　善人も悪人も選ばず殺す。

　信じられない。
　信じたくない。

　だが、疑えなかった。
　彼の自白は、虚言にしては重過ぎた。

　それが事実。
　
　……わけがわからない。

　いっそ、全部投げ出してしまいたかった。
　何もかも忘れて。どこか別の街で一から出直したい。

　そうしたところで、誰にも責められはしないだろう。

　ならば……
　それは、できるだろうか。

　綾弥一条に。
　それは、できる事だろうか。

　無理だ。

She remembered her father's <ruby>stench of decay<rt>・・</rt></ruby>.
She remembered her father's <ruby>sneering laugh<rt>・・</rt></ruby>.

Ichijou Ayane knew Ichidou Ayane. She knew what it meant to be his daughter.

Therefore she could never run.

Not from the fight against unforgivable evil.
Not from the pursuit of justice.

Not from Kageaki Minato.

Not from the confrontation with the man who had poured light on her road.
